procedure_text: A mixture of enol ester (20g, 0.06mol) and dichloromethane (60mL) taken in a clean, pre-dried 250mL round bottomed flask and cooled to 10-15°C. To this mixture, added sodium cyanide (1.2g, 0.025mol) followed by slow addition of triethylamine (6.6g, 0.065mol) for 15-20mins at 10-15°C under stirring. The reaction mixture is cooled at 10-15°C and maintained for about 2 hours and quenched with water (100mL). Dichloromethane was separated through distillation under reduced pressure at 35-45°C. The aqueous mass obtained was cooled to 5-10°C and acidified to pH < 3 using aqueous hydrochloric acid (5.4mL, 0.054mol). The precipitated product obtained was separated through filtration, washed with water (60 mL) and dried under reduced pressure to obtain mesotrione as yellow to tan colour solid. HPLC purity >95%; Yield: 17g (85%); Melting point of the solid was 155-157°C;and solvent recovery: > 85%.
procedure_summary: The enol ester of formula (II) is converted to mesotrione in dichloromethane at reduced temperature, sodium cyanide being charged first and triethylamine then added slowly, and the mixture held cold before being quenched with water. The dichloromethane is distilled off under reduced pressure, the cooled aqueous mass is acidified with aqueous hydrochloric acid to precipitate the product, and the solid is filtered, washed with water and dried under reduced pressure.

REACTION CLASS. Recorded as acylation with medium confidence, and the alternative is recorded here rather than hidden. What happens is an intramolecular migration of the 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoyl group from the enol oxygen of the ester to C2 of the cyclohexane-1,3-dione ring, promoted by cyanide with triethylamine as base. Reactant and product are isomers, both C14H13NO7S, so by conservation of formula the step is an isomerisation and the most precise single word for it is rearrangement. The prompt's reaction_class enumeration has no rearrangement or isomerisation member. acylation was chosen because it names the bond actually formed, a carbon-carbon bond to an acyl group at the dione 2-position, and it is the class an automated extractor would most plausibly reach for the same transformation; other was the alternative and would have carried less information. Confidence is medium for that reason and not because the chemistry is unclear. Both readings are carried in the tags, transformation:rearrangement and transformation:acylation.

MECHANISM. ionic. Cyanide is a nucleophile and triethylamine deprotonates, so the intermediates on any reasonable reading of this step are anionic. catalytic was considered and rejected: the sodium cyanide charge is 0.025 mol against 0.06 mol of enol ester, so it is sub-stoichiometric and a catalytic reading is available, but the text does not call it a catalyst and does not describe recovering or recycling it. A1 recorded its role as reagent for the same reason and this record agrees.
